items.body:
MAINZ. **In den Pausen sollen Kinder und Jugendliche spielen oder mehr miteinander sprechen, statt Nachrichten zu schreiben – meint die rheinland-pfälzische Bildungsministerin. Sie hat dafür neue Regeln für den Gebrauch von Handys in Schulen erlassen. Recht strenge: Bis einschließlich 10. Klasse gilt bald für Schülerinnen und Schüler ein Verbot privater Nutzung von Smartphones. Die Schülervertretung zeigt sich wenig begeistert.**

Und – weg. (Symbolfoto) Foto: Shutterstock

Handys, iPads, Smartwatches und Smartbrillen sind für Schülerinnen und Schüler bis Ende der 10. Klasse ab dem zweiten Halbjahr an den Schulen in Rheinland-Pfalz für die private Nutzung tabu. Bei der Regelung gehe es um internetfähige digitale Endgeräte, sagte Bildungsministerin Ute Eiling-Hütig (CDU) in Mainz.

Ausnahmen gebe es, wenn die Smartphones und iPads für Lehr- und Lernzwecke verwendet werden, aus gesundheitlichen Gründen sowie etwa auf Klassenfahrten, wenn die Kinder und Jugendlichen dringend bei ihren Eltern anrufen möchten. Das entschieden dann die betreuenden Lehrkräfte, erklärte Eiling-Hütig.

## Mittagspause regeln die Schulen

In die Entscheidung der Schulen falle auch die private Nutzung der internetfähigen digitalen Endgeräte in der Mittagspause beim Ganztag. Ansonsten gelte auch für den schulischen Nachmittag das private Handy-Verbot, sagte die Bildungsministerin.

Ob die Schülerinnen und Schüler ihre Geräte abgeben und etwa in einen Spind packen müssen oder ausgeschaltet in der Tasche haben, liege dann im Ermessen der Schulen. Da mache das Bildungsministerium keine Vorgaben, sagte die CDU-Politikerin.

## Berufliche Schulen signalisieren auch Interesse

Das Vorhaben gelte auch für die Förderschulen in Rheinland-Pfalz. Die beruflichen Schulen seien nicht dabei. Es gebe aber bereits positive Rückmeldungen mit Interesse für eine Einführung der Handy-Regeln. Bei den Oberstufen werde es genauso gehandhabt wie mit der Mittagspause, erklärte Eiling-Hütig: Es liege in der Entscheidung der Schulen.

Die finale detaillierte Umsetzung der neuen Regeln werde nach Abschluss der Verbändeanhörung festgelegt. Innerhalb der Koalition mit der SPD seien die Beschlüsse kein großes Streitthema gewesen, versicherte die Christdemokratin.

## Landesschülervertretung weiter gegen Handy-Verbot

Die Landeschülerinnen und -schülervertretung (LSV) spricht sich nach Angaben der Ministerin weiterhin gegen die Maßnahmen aus. Ein pauschales Verbot greife zu kurz und ersetze keine pädagogischen Konzepte, argumentierte zuletzt die LSV. Die Kinder und Jugendlichen müssten lernen, verantwortungsvoll mit digitalen Medien umzugehen. Dafür brauche es eine stärkere Verankerung von Medienbildung und klare, gemeinsam entwickelte Regeln an Schulen.

Cybermobbing, problematische Inhalte oder exzessive Mediennutzung dürften nicht ignoriert werden. Doch pauschalen Handy-Verbote an Schulen sowie mögliche Social-Media-Verboten seien keine nachhaltige Lösung, mahnte die LSV. Sie beseitigten die Ursachen nicht, sondern würden die Probleme lediglich aus dem Blickfeld verschieben. Cybermobbing mache nicht vor der Schule halt und verschwinde nicht, wenn das Smartphone in die Tasche stecke.

## Vorbildfunktion für zu Hause

Der Landesregierung sei wichtig, dass sich die Kinder in den Pausen einfach in Präsenz miteinander beschäftigen. Es gehe um das Vertiefen der sozialen Kompetenzen. «Ich muss meiner Freundin vielleicht nicht eine WhatsApp schreiben, die zwei Meter weiter steht, sondern ich kann direkt mit ihr sprechen.»

Eiling-Hütig äußerte die Hoffnung, dass die neuen Handy-Regeln auch eine Vorbildfunktion für das Nutzungsverhalten der Kinder und Jugendlichen in der Freizeit hat. Eltern könnten dann argumentieren, dass das Weglegen der Smartphones und iPads zu Hause genauso wie in der Schule funktionieren könne.

## Plattformbetreiber im Fokus

Die Bildungsministerin sprach sich in der Diskussion über ein Social-Media-Verbot für bestimmte Altersgruppen dafür aus, die Plattformen mehr in die Verantwortung zu nehmen. Es könne nicht alleine die Aufgabe der Politik, der Eltern, Lehrkräfte sowie der Schülerinnen und Schüler sein, für Regelungen zu sorgen. Stattdessen müssten die Plattformbetreiber mehr in die Verpflichtung genommen werden. *News4teachers / mit Material der dpa*

> [Handy-Verbote reichen nicht: Leopoldina warnt vor Social-Media-Risiken – und fordert mehr Medienerziehung in Kitas und Schulen](https://www.news4teachers.de/2025/08/handy-verbote-allein-schuetzen-nicht-leopoldina-warnt-vor-social-media-risiken-und-fordert-mehr-medienkompetenz-in-kitas-und-schulen/)

items.body:
# opt.in.ismus

Deadline: 05.01.2027

## opt.in.ismus

## Call for Particitpation für die re:publica 27 vom 10. bis 12. Mai 2027 in Berlin. Deadline: 5. Januar 2027

Es ist wieder soweit: Der Call for Participation zur re:publica 27 ist geöffnet!

Du hast eine Idee, ein Projekt, eine Recherche, ein Experiment oder eine künstlerische Intervention, die die digitale Gesellschaft voranbringt und im #rp27-Programm nicht fehlen darf? Dann bist du hier genau richtig – denn ohne dich und deine Idee wäre das re:publica-Programm nicht das, was es ist.

Vom 10.-12. Mai 2027 verwandeln wir die STATION Berlin in einen Ort für Austausch, Begegnungen, Debatten, Kunst und viele Überraschungen – und das bereits zum 20. Mal.

Sei dabei und gestalte die #rp27 mit!

Jetzt beim CfP einreichen

Warum du mitmachen solltest

Die re:publica lebt von euren Perspektiven. Von Menschen, die etwas zu sagen haben, die hinterfragen, um die Ecke denken, forschen, gestalten oder Debatten anstoßen. Von denen, die Projekte anschieben und umsetzen, Communities aufbauen oder Kunst schaffen, die berührt und zum Mitmachen einlädt. Wir freuen uns auf deine Expertise, deine Stimme, deine Kreativität – egal ob du zum ersten Mal dabei bist oder schon lange Teil der re:publica-Community.

Welche Formate du einreichen kannst

Für den Konferenzbereich kannst du folgende Formate einreichen:

- (Kurz-)Vortrag – Präsentationen zu einem Thema, allein oder zu zweit.
- Gespräch – Dialog oder Streitgespräch, mit oder ohne Moderation.
- Podiumsdiskussion – Moderiertes Gespräch mit verschiedenen Perspektiven.
- Podcast – Dein bestehender Podcast auf unserer Bühne.
- Meet Up – Offenes Treffen für Austausch mit der Community.
- Rede mit! – Interaktive oder dialogorientierte Formate wie Fishbowl.
- Workshop – Praktisch-partizipative Sessions zum Mitmachen.
- Nightlife – Kunst und Unterhaltung für die späteren Stunden!
- Embodiment – Körperbasierte Formate wie Bewegung oder Meditation.
- Sonderformat – Alles, was in keine Schublade passt.
Für den Off-Stage-Bereich kannst du folgende Formate einreichen:

- Installationen – Interaktive Arbeiten auf dem Festivalgelände.
- Spiele – Digitale oder analoge Games.
- Interventionen – Aktionen, die Raum und Publikum einbeziehen.
- DIY/Maker-Projekte – Mitmach-Formate und Projekte zum Ausprobieren.
- Sonderformate – Alles Ungewöhnliche und Überraschende.
Worauf es bei der Einreichung ankommt

Wichtig ist, dass dein Beitrag die Themen der digitalen Gesellschaft weiterdenkt: Von kritischen Fragen über neue Visionen bis zu konkreten Lösungen. Ob gesellschaftspolitisch, künstlerisch, technisch, wissenschaftlich, aktivistisch oder ganz persönlich – wir freuen uns auf deine Ideen, Perspektiven und Projekte!

Was uns besonders überzeugt:

- Relevanz, Aktualität & Lösungsorientierung
- Eigene Haltung und klare Perspektive
- Mehrwert für unser Publikum
- Vielfalt und Sichtbarkeit verschiedener Stimmen
Was uns nicht überzeugt:

- Marketing oder Sales-Pitch
- Buzzwords ohne Substanz
Das re:publica 27-Motto: #optinism

Opt-in heißt: bewusst Ja sagen, sich für etwas entscheiden. Optimismus heißt: daran glauben, dass Veränderung zum Positiven möglich ist. Zusammen wird daraus unser Motto für die re:publica 2027 .

Wir wollen mit euch diskutieren, experimentieren, streiten und neue Perspektiven entdecken. Denn nach 20 Jahren re:publica wissen wir: Eine bessere Zukunft fällt nicht vom Himmel. Sie braucht Menschen, die sich einmischen, Dinge hinterfragen und einfach mal anfangen.

Das Motto ist dabei unser gedanklicher Rahmen, keine thematische Schublade. Deine Einreichung muss sich nicht ausdrücklich auf das Motto beziehen.

Weitere Inspiration findest du in unseren diesjährigen Tracks und Schwerpunkt-Themen , oder du schaust dir die zahlreichen Videomitschnitte vergangener re:publica-Festivals auf unserem YouTube-Kanal an.

Alles, was du für deine Einreichung wissen musst, haben wir hier für dich zusammengestellt:

Hier geht's zum CfP

Solltest du weitere Fragen haben, schau doch gern in unsere FAQ .

Deadline: Der Call for Participation für das Programm der re:publica Berlin 2027 endet am 05.01.2027 (23:59 Uhr MEZ).

Mach mit – und gestalte die re:publica 27 mit uns!

Wir freuen uns auf deinen Beitrag.

Zur Ausschreibung (Link)

# Uganda Buddhist Centre campaign passes $1 million; new short film released

- Uganda Buddhist Centre campaign passes $1 million; new short film released | Lion’s Roar Uganda Buddhist Centre campaign passes $1 million; new short film released Supporters are halfway to the $2 million goal for protecting a Lake Victoria wetland and building Africa’s first dedicated retreat center, with $750,000 still needed by December 15. Rod Meade Sperry 25 November 2026 Bhante Buddharakkhita with His Holiness the Dalai Lama, who encouraged Bhante to pursue his vision for UBC. As seen in the new “Find Friends” video. Share Share Options
- Copy Link
- Facebook
- Email
The campaign to secure land for the Uganda Buddhist Centre (UBC) has passed $1 million, putting it halfway to its $2 million goal, organizers announced this week. Another $750,000 is needed to complete the land purchase by the December 15 deadline .

“What we do in the next three weeks decides whether this land is protected forever,” campaign organizer Leslie Booker wrote in the announcement.

### The story so far

Lion’s Roar first reported on the campaign in August, as UBC marked its 20th anniversary. Founded in 2005 by Bhante Buddharakkhita, UBC was the first Buddhist center in Uganda and the first in Africa established by an African monk. Its campus in Bulega-Garuga, near Entebbe, includes the Buddhist Peace School, the African Buddhist High School, and a medical center serving the surrounding community.

The campaign aims to buy 13 acres of wetland next to the campus, on the shores of Lake Nalubaale (Lake Victoria), the source of the Nile. Bhante Buddharakkhita plans to build what organizers describe as the first retreat center on the African continent dedicated solely to sharing the dhamma, and to protect the wetland permanently. If the land isn’t secured, it could be sold for a resort or a military base. Organizers warn that either would threaten food and water security for nearby schools, an orphanage, and surrounding villages.

In September, we reported that supporters had paid the $875,000 deposit needed to hold the land, and that the seller had extended the deadline for the remaining balance to December 15.

### “ Halfway home “

The $1.75 million asking price makes up most of the campaign’s $2 million goal. The rest covers surveys and unexpected costs. With $1 million raised, the $750,000 still needed by December 15 would complete the purchase itself.

Booker credited the campaign’s community for the milestone, saying every dollar came “from people like you,” through gifts large and small and through supporters sharing the campaign with others. Organizers are asking for “gratitude gifts” over the Thanksgiving week, whether it’s a donor’s first gift or their fifth. They’re also asking supporters to share the campaign with friends.

### A new film

The campaign has also released a short film, Find Friends: Bhante Buddharakkhita and the Uganda Buddhist Centre . It tells the story of UBC, Bhante Buddharakkhita’s vision for the land, and why protecting it matters. The film features Bhante Buddharakkhita and Booker.

“If you’ve ever tried to explain what Bhante means to you and couldn’t find the words, this film does it for you,” Booker wrote.

### How to help

Donations can be made through the campaign’s Chuffed page . Gifts are tax-deductible in the US. Donor-advised fund grants and employer matching gifts are also accepted. Supporters can also start a fundraising team with their sangha or friends through the same page.

Rod Meade Sperry

items.body:
The home page of Salon’s website in November 1999.

In the dying days of 1995, I was a freelance journalist in Portland, Oregon, who spent most of my time seated at a rickety particle-board desk, a gift from my father-in-law. The desk was covered in faux-walnut laminate and swayed from side to side as I wrote. I had already finished my main financial gusher for that year, a history book for fifth graders, and I needed more work.

In this respect I was no different than any freelancer in literary history. In fact, the technology involved in my trade, and the speed at which it functioned—its industrial metabolism—had hardly changed in the preceding century. Of course, I had a computer. But it hardly seemed to be much more than a glorified typewriter. And of course I had an email account, courtesy of the nerd Valhalla known as CompuServe. But the business of freelance journalism was still built largely around stuffing wads of paper into envelopes and sending them to editors, who would then transform the contents into other wads of paper: newspapers, magazines, books. The product, whatever you thought of it, was palpable.

Into this cozy Victorian setting came an online publication called Salon. It had been launched that same fall by a crew of ex-staffers from the San Francisco Examiner, traditional journalists trying to break the mold. I don’t remember which Salon editor contacted me in the first place. I do remember reading the website in my chilly little office, steadying the stupid desk with one leg and feeling an almost metaphysical puzzlement. Salon wasn’t some programmer’s hobby, whipped up in creaky old COBOL. It looked like a magazine, with zippy graphics and respectable fonts. The prose was smart, stylish, and amusingly contrarian.

All of this made a kind of sense to me. What was tricky was that it was free. That first afternoon, I printed out one of the articles, about The Beatles Anthology, which was just then airing on TV. I suppose I was turning back the technological clock—transubstantiating the product back into paper. Reading Salon gratis made me feel as if I were doing something furtive, as though I were a shoplifter, but it represented a kind of post-Gutenberg freedom.

Over the next year, I would write many pieces for Salon. I started out with book reviews that were assigned to me by Dwight Garner. (He had previously edited a few things of mine at Vogue, in terms of ethos the absolute inverse of Salon and, eventually, in terms of finances too.) Dwight sent me books by the bushel, or so it felt. I wrote very short pieces for him very quickly; they appeared online almost immediately. This, for the journalist, was unprecedented and nearly beggared belief. No more waiting for your piece to come out, pacing the equivalent of a widow’s walk. Sometimes I was even instructed to send the piece straight to the copy editor so we could cut a few more minutes out of the process.

Speediness of reflexes was part of the value proposition for Salon. Within months, the “smart tabloid,” as its founder David Talbot called it, was posting daily rather than weekly. In this way it inaugurated a fire hose style of journalism that would in time become universal. The new norm was not waiting, not allowing stories to lose their heat in the cooling saucer of classic media.

Salon’s politics were similarly nontraditional: left-leaning, libertarian-adjacent (as per its Bay Area digs), but without an obvious party line. It doubtless helped that the magazine was not a subsidiary of a larger corporation, which was the case with Slate (part of Microsoft) and the earlier, cruder Mr. Showbiz (part of Starwave, a short-lived multimedia platform founded by Microsoft’s Paul Allen). Yes, Salon’s seed funding had come from Apple—a mingy $60,000—followed by a more substantial disbursement to the tune of $2 million from the Adobe cofounder John Warnock and various other investors. But it was an independent entity, unconstrained by the need to tiptoe around the feelings of a corporate proprietor.

In any case, I wasn’t writing about politics. I was writing about culture: the magazine’s strong suit. From books I branched into music—I believe it was Joyce Millman, Salon’s television critic, who assigned me pieces about Prince, Los Lobos, Bill Frisell, Cassandra Wilson. These were my enthusiasms, not the sort of dutiful, indiscriminate coverage that a film-critic friend of mine once likened to servicing a vending machine. I was allowed to venture further still when I pitched a piece about Martin Scorsese’s use of music. (The Casino soundtrack, I wrote, struck me as what the director might listen to “if he were shipwrecked with nothing but a polyester suit and a bank of slot machines.”)

It wasn’t long before I was writing short personal essays. I wrote one about being hoaxed by the founder of the Church of Kurt Cobain, which turned out to be nonexistent, although certainly plausible in the drizzling, grunge-friendly atmosphere of Portland. I wrote another about becoming addicted to All My Children during a serious family health crisis in the midst of which I found myself strangely inspired by the surreal resiliency of the characters, who never died unless their respective actor’s contracts with the show expired. I’m not making any extreme claims for these pieces. They were written at the madcap pace dictated by Salon and sandwiched between other freelance explorations—of dental malocclusion or aluminum smelting, say. For me, though, they still evoke the adrenaline feel of the period, the wild sense of participating in something new and transformative.

…

## Art Basel Announces New Highlights To Look Forward to at 2026 Miami Beach

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/art-basel-miami-beach-2026-highlights/)

Art Basel Miami Beach, General Impressions, Courtesy of Art Basel

[Art Basel Miami Beach](https://mymodernmet.com/art-basel-miami-beach-2025-recap/) is preparing to bring the international art world together for another year. The fair has announced additional details for its 2026 edition, including major gallery presentations, digital art projects, artist conversations, and public installations throughout South Florida. With 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories, the event will offer a wide-ranging look at contemporary art and the ideas shaping it.

The newly announced gallery presentations span several generations and mediums. Brazilian artist Rosana Paulino will present her first bronze sculpture, *Crisálida* (2025–26), with Mendes Wood DM. Other highlights include a new painting by Shara Hughes at David Kordansky Gallery and monumental bronze sculpture by Wangechi Mutu at Gladstone. A joint presentation by Ortuzar and Crèvecœur will feature paintings by Ernie Barnes, coinciding with an exhibition of his work at ICA Miami. Miami-based Spinello Projects will also make its debut in the Galleries sector, showcasing artists from the Latin American and Caribbean diaspora.

Digital art will have an expanded presence through Zero 10: Generation, the initiative’s largest edition to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, it brings together 21 exhibitors across 19 projects. The presentations explore generative art, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies. The program also looks to the history of digital experimentation, with a presentation on early computer art in Latin America and a new collaboration with Google Arts & Culture.

The fair’s Conversations program will explore the connections between art and other cultural fields, including sports and technology. Across four days, artists, curators, and public figures will discuss topics ranging from creative practice to identity and representation.

A dedicated Art & Sports series features NBA champion Kevin Love, soccer star Crystal Dunn, and Brooklyn Nets and New York Liberty co-owner Clara Wu Tsai. The program also includes a panel with the NFL examining portraiture and legacy in professional football.

Beyond the convention center, public art and museum exhibitions will extend the experience across Greater Miami. In Collins Park, *Between Tides*, a collaboration with Public Art Fund, transforms six ping-pong tables into playable sculptural installations designed by artists.

The Art Basel Awards will also return for a second year, recognizing achievements across the contemporary art world. The winners will be announced at a ceremony at Miami Beach’s New World Center.

Art Basel Miami Beach takes place Dec. 4–6, at the Miami Beach Convention Center. VIP preview days are scheduled for December 2–3.

## Art Basel Miami Beach returns with 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories.

items.body:
# Shamash Alidina: Gratitude with Room for Everything Else

Gratitude practices sometimes feel like one more thing to get right, as if we’re supposed to feel thankful on cue no matter what’s happening.

Our guest this week is Shamash Alidina. He offers a gentler approach. You make room for whatever you’re feeling, and then you see whether one small, ordinary thing you appreciate can sit alongside it.

In this meditation, you’ll:

- Acknowledge how life is for you right now
- Hold difficulty and appreciation side by side
- Connect gratitude to what you value, rather than just how you feel
## Shamash Alidina: Gratitude with Room for Everything Else

Read and practice this meditation on your own, pausing after each step. Or listen to the guided audio.

- Find a comfortable position and let your body settle. You can close your eyes or keep them open with a soft, relaxed gaze. There’s nothing to achieve here. You don’t need to feel calm, happy, or grateful. You’re simply giving yourself a little time to be here.
- Notice the places where your body makes contact with what’s beneath you. Feel the gentle movement of your breath. There’s no need to change it. Just notice the body breathing in and breathing out.
- Allow whatever you’re experiencing to be here. Maybe your mind is busy or your body feels restless. That’s fine. There’s nothing you need to fix.
- Bring to mind how life is for you at the moment. Perhaps something is worrying you. Maybe you’re missing someone, feeling lonely, or facing a challenge. Or perhaps things are going reasonably well. Whatever you notice, acknowledge it honestly. You might silently say, This is what I’m experiencing right now.
- Notice any feeling in your body that comes with this experience. It might be tightness, heaviness, or restlessness. You don’t need to make it go away. Imagine making room for it the way you’d make room for a visitor at your door. You don’t have to invite it to stay forever. Just acknowledge that it’s here. For these few moments, there’s no need to talk yourself out of how you feel. Let yourself be a human being with human experiences.
- With the difficulty in the background, look for one small thing you appreciate. It might be someone who cares about you, a place where you feel safe, a warm drink, a comfortable bed, or a memory of laughter. Something quite ordinary is enough. If nothing comes to mind, that’s perfectly fine. Simply notice the support beneath your body or feel your feet on the floor. You don’t have to produce gratitude on demand.
- If you’ve found something, take a little time with it. What about this person, place, or experience matters to you? Maybe it brings warmth, comfort, connection, or relief. Maybe it’s simply pleasant. Don’t force the feeling to be bigger than it is.
- Notice the details. If it’s a memory, recall it gently. If it’s happening now, explore it through your senses. Let yourself receive the experience rather than hurrying on to the next thing.
- Hold both the difficult and the good. You don’t need to get rid of a difficult feeling to appreciate something good. You can feel worried and still enjoy being supported. You can feel sad and remember someone you love. You can feel lonely and appreciate a small, kind interaction. Imagine holding the difficulty in one hand and this small appreciation in the other.
- Consider what this moment of appreciation points toward. Is there something you value in it, such as connection, kindness, friendship, health, creativity, or a little space to stop and breathe? Is there one small action you could take today to bring more of it into your life? You could send someone a message, step outside, take a proper break, or offer yourself a little more patience. If today is hard, the kindest thing may be to allow yourself some rest or support. Gratitude doesn’t require you to pretend everything is fine.
- Return to your surroundings. Notice your breathing, the sounds around you, and the support beneath your body. When you’re ready, gently open your eyes if they’ve been closed, and bring some gentle movement into your body.
- Thank yourself for taking these few minutes. May you find room for both the difficult moments and the small moments of goodness in the days ahead.
### About The Author

### Shamash Alidina

Shamash Alidina has been practising mindfulness since 1998 and runs his own successful training organisation. He is the author of Mindfulness For Dummies and most recently, The Mindful Way Through Stress . He frequently pops up in newspapers, magazines and on radio shows. Based in London, he runs online trainings and speaks at conferences all over the world. He’s been teaching mindfulness full-time since 2010.

items.feedText: Interestingly, this optimistic narrative overlooks a challenge that is becoming increasingly apparent in aging neuroscience: brain health depends critically on a continuous supply of trophic signals originating from skeletal muscle and bone. Myokines and osteokines such as irisin, uncarboxylated osteocalcin, and cathepsin B act on the brain to sustain BDNF expression, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis, forming what has been described as a muscle-bone-brain axis; disuse and immobilization, even in the absence…
items.body: Advances in brain-machine interfaces and neuroprosthetics are often framed as a path toward overcoming the biological limits of the body, with the eventual replacement of failing limbs and organs by durable artificial substitutes. Interestingly, this optimistic narrative overlooks a challenge that is becoming increasingly apparent in aging neuroscience: brain health depends critically on a continuous supply of trophic signals originating from skeletal muscle and bone. Myokines and osteokines such as irisin, uncarboxylated osteocalcin, and cathepsin B act on the brain to sustain BDNF expression, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis, forming what has been described as a muscle-bone-brain axis; disuse and immobilization, even in the absence of any primary brain pathology, are sufficient to disrupt this signaling and accelerate cognitive decline. This raises a largely unaddressed question for cyborg technologies: could a robotic body, mechanically capable of movement but biologically inert and secreting none of the trophic factors that living muscle and bone normally provide, deprive the brain of signals it needs to remain healthy, thereby accelerating, rather than preventing, neural aging? We term this hypothetical condition cyborg dementia. Rather than a purely engineering problem of motor control and sensory feedback, this reframes brain-machine interface design as fundamentally about preserving the endocrine dialogue between brain and musculoskeletal system, extending the goals of neuroprosthetics beyond restoring action to protecting the neuroendocrine mechanisms that biological embodiment was silently providing all along.

## The Map of Ancient Philosophy: Animation Shows How Socrates, Aristotle, Confucius, the Buddha & Other Great Thinkers Fit Together

in History , Maps , Philosophy | November 25th, 2026 Leave a Comment

-->

Here on Open Cul­ture, we’ve often fea­tured the charm­ing and infor­ma­tive posters of Domain of Sci­ence . Each one maps out a dif­fer­ent field of knowl­edge: there’s biol­o­gy , physics , chem­istry , quan­tum physics , quan­tum com­put­ing , fun­gi , and many oth­ers besides. But with his lat­est map, Domain of Sci­ence cre­ator Dominic Wal­li­man has turned away from the sci­en­tif­ic realm — or rather, he’s ven­tured into the larg­er intel­lec­tu­al ter­ri­to­ry out of which it emerged. His new Map of Phi­los­o­phy , which he explains in the video above , includes schools of thought going all the way back to 600 BC, and thinkers from antiq­ui­ty like Thales, Laozi, Con­fu­cius, and the Bud­dha, who lived and died before sci­ence as we know it.

That hard­ly means that they’ve become irrel­e­vant today. There still exist soci­eties described as Con­fu­cian or Bud­dhist, of course, but in the West­ern world, we’re more like­ly to refer back to — and, in many cas­es, have read a bit of — the work of Socrates, Pla­to, and Aris­to­tle. “They basi­cal­ly laid the intel­lec­tu­al foun­da­tion of West­ern phi­los­o­phy, sci­ence, and polit­i­cal thought,” says Wal­li­man. (He also reminds us that it was Socrates who said that the unex­am­ined life is not worth liv­ing, which “hits pret­ty hard in the age of the dis­trac­tion econ­o­my.”)

Though often men­tioned togeth­er, these three ancient Greeks occu­py slight­ly dif­fer­ent posi­tions on the philo­soph­i­cal map, with Socrates clos­er to the land of ethics, Pla­to to meta­physics, and Aris­to­tle to epis­te­mol­o­gy.

As Wal­li­man explains, “epis­te­mol­o­gy stud­ies knowl­edge: what it is, where it comes from, and also how it dif­fers from faith or opin­ions,” while also seek­ing out its lim­its. Aris­totle’s rig­or in test­ing and orga­niz­ing knowl­edge makes him, in a sense, one of the ear­li­est sci­en­tists. Though his body of the­o­ry may no longer be our best means of under­stand­ing how the world works, his sys­tem­at­ic pur­suit of such an under­stand­ing set him apart from much of the ancient intel­lec­tu­al world. The islands off the coast of the map’s main­land rep­re­sent sub­fields still active­ly explored today, like the philoso­phies of mind, lan­guage, pol­i­tics, reli­gion, and sci­ence — which, for all its pres­tige, remains as sub­ject to philo­soph­i­cal inquiry as any oth­er area of human endeav­or. The map of phi­los­o­phy shows us not a rar­efied, most­ly aban­doned ter­ri­to­ry, but the place where we all live our lives, exam­ined or oth­er­wise.

Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly [Opportunities Newsletter](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/).

**[Fall $1,800 Innovate Grants for Art + Photo](https://innovateartistgrants.org)** **Featured**
Innovate Grant awards two $1,800 grants each quarter to one visual artist and one photographer. Nine honorable mentions in each category are also featured on the Innovate Grant platform and join a growing creative community of esteemed artists. Applicants must be 18 years and older, and all media and genres are accepted. All applicants retain the right to the work they submit.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on December 15, 2026.**

**[Bryson County Retreat](https://www.brysoncountyretreat.org/)** **Featured**
Practicing artists of any background and at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply for a 2027 residency at Bryson County Retreat. Residency periods can be flexible, but month-long stays are suggested. Bryson County is designed to provide ample living and working space and inspirational settings where an artist may work free from the distractions and responsibilities of day-to-day life. The program includes free lodging near tannic dark water lakes, sprawling live oaks, and drooping Spanish moss at the headwaters of the Santa Fe River in north central Florida.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**Open Calls**

**[Wildlife Photographer of the Year](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/wildlife-photographer-of-the-year/competition.html)** *(International)*
Alongside its conservation message, this prestigious global competition is hosted by London’s Natural History Museum to champion the work of photographers, whether professional or amateur, young or older, or using top-of-the-range equipment or smartphones. Photographers are eligible for myriad awards, with a Grand Title prize of £15,000. The entry fee is £35 (free for Young WPY contest).
**Deadline: 11:30 p.m. GMT on December 3, 2026.**

**[Responsa Foundation Open Call for Textile Art](https://responsafoundation.com/2026/10/13/this-memory-competition/)** *(International)*
The Responsa Foundation champions projects that create meaningful social impact and foster public engagement. The organization is seeking textile artists to submit work for *This Memory,* a group exhibition taking place from September 22 to October 3, 2027, at Burgh House in Hampstead.
**Deadline: December 4, 2026.**

**[Open Call for Public Art Proposals in Moab](https://www.moabarts.org/public-art-application)** (Utah, National)
Moab Arts is accepting proposals for 2027 public art projects. Proposals are welcome for sculpture, murals, three crosswalks, and sticker designs but may include other ideas for different media or locations around the city. Preference is given to local and regional artists.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MST on December 6, 2026.**

**[Material Works Art Award 2026](https://pci.jotform.com/form/262185636090156)** *(International)*
Material Works supports artists through one-time $2,500 awards in exchange for original pieces added to its growing contemporary art collection. The award recognizes artistic excellence and aims to promote career advancement through increasing visibility and exposure. There is a €40 application fee.
**Deadline: December 6, 2026, or when the first 300 artworks submitted, whichever comes first.**

**[Call for Mail Art](https://www.hivebookarts.org/exhibitions/call-for-mail-art)** *(International)*
Hive Center for the Book Arts in Evanston, Illinois, welcomes mail art for the exhibition *love|mark*, which runs from January 1 to February 27. All submissions must arrive at at the center by December 15 for inclusion in the show.
**Deadline:** **December 15, 2026.**

items.body:
**Das brandneue** **Elektron Tonverk 1.5-** **Update bringt den Performance-Sampler auf das nächste Level.** **Einen ganzen Stapel von neuen Features erwarten die User. Laut Elektron ist dies das bisher größte Update, das die Schweden bisher abgeliefert haben.**

## Alles über die Updates für Elektron Tonverk

- Das Elektron Tonverk 1.5-Update ist da Zwei neue Maschinen
- Neue Effekte
- Weitere Neuheiten im 1.5-Update für Elektron Tonverk
- Verfügbarkeit und Preis
- Weitere Infos

## Das Elektron Tonverk 1.5-Update ist da

Elektron Tonverk · Quelle: Elektron

Neue Maschinen, neue Effekte, verbesserter Workflow und erweiterte MIDI-Funktionen. Das alles steckt in dem 1.5-Update für Elektron Tonverk, das ab sofort verfügbar ist. Gehen wir mal die Neuheiten durch.

Kurzer Rückblick: Mit 1.0.1 gab es die ersten Bugfixes. 1.1.0 brachte mit Grainer und Shape Granular-Synthese und neue Filterparameter. 1.2.0 lieferte einen neuen Reverb und den Filter-Folder für neue Klangfarben. Wavetables zogen mit dem 1.3-Update ein und dazu ein paar weitere Optimierungen. 1.4 erfreute mit der langerwarteten Overbridge-Integration (die immer noch nicht ganz ausgreift ist) sowie neuen Möglichkeiten für Modulation und ein paar weiteren Verbesserungen.

Jetzt steht 1.5 an und damit wird Elektron Tonverk an vielen Stellen um Funktionen erweitert.

### Zwei neue Maschinen

Zwei Maschinen gibt es jetzt. Stretcher bringt Time-Stretching in den Performance-Sampler und kombiniert das mit Pitch-Shifting. Samples und Loops können so nicht nur einfacher angepasst, sondern auch im Sound verändert werden. Dafür stehen diverse Parameter und verschiedene Algorithmen bereit. Sehr cool! Elektron feiert das mit neuen kostenlosen Samples, die zeitnah erscheinen sollen.

Waveswarmer bringt eine Art von Super-Saw in den Sampler. Aber eben etwas anders! Ein Cluster von verstimmten Wavetables erzeugt den „Schwarm“ und natürlich können Position und Bewegung der Wavetables gesteuert werden. Phase-Modulation, zusätzliches Rauschen und weitere Goodies machen daraus eine schöne neue Engine.

### Neue Effekte

Neue Effekte bekommt Elektron Tonverk ebenfalls mit dem Update. Pulse Gate FX erzeugen Effekte, die einige als Trance-Gate bezeichnen. Über sequenzierte Hüllkurven wird Audio rhythmisch zerhackt.

Für mehr Punch oder Körper sorgen die Transient Control FX – dahinter steckt also ein Transient Shaper. Auch sehr willkommen! Zwei neue EQs gehören ebenso zu dem Update: Einer für den Channel oder auch Busse und Mixe, Parametric EQ bietet mehr chirurgische Eingeriffe.

### Weitere Neuheiten im 1.5-Update für Elektron Tonverk

Die Subtracks Machine bietet jetzt die Möglichkeit, einem einzelnen Subtrack einen eigenen Signalweg zuweisen und Send- sowie Insert-Effekte individuell einsetzen. So kannst du beispielsweise die Snare mit Reverb versehen, während die Kickdrum trocken bleibt.

Praktisch ist auch der neue Multisample-Editor, um Samples komfortabler direkt am Elektron Tonverk zu editieren. Der Hersteller verspricht dafür aber auch zusätzlich eine browserbasierte Version – einfach weil der Bildschirm an der Hardware dann doch etwas zu klein für solche Aufgaben ist. Dieser Editor soll dann als erste Erweiterung von Elektron Labb erscheinen. Demnächst!

Tonverk kann jetzt als MIDI-Host fungieren! USB-MIDI-Geräte können direkt angeschlossen und mit Storm (bis zu 500 mA bei 5 V) versorgt werden, ohne einen Rechner dazwischengeschaltet zu haben.

Als weitere Neuheiten bietet das Update: Unison mit Detune und Panorama-Spreading, Send-Tracks mit Arpeggiator-, Transpose- und MIDI-Funktionalität (!), einen Wavetable-Generator und ein paar weitere Verbesserungen.

Ein echt starkes Update, das ab sofort kostenlos zur Verfügung steht. Hier auf der [Website von Elektron](https://www.elektronauts.com/news/639) findest du weitere Infos.

items.body:
# WhatsApp launches highly requested new feature for sending messages later - 9to5Mac

## WhatsApp launches highly requested new feature for sending messages later

WhatsApp just announced that it is rolling out scheduled messages, which it says is one of users’ most requested features. Here are the details.

## Here’s how to send a scheduled message in WhatsApp

From WhatsApp’s blog post announcing support for scheduled messages:

> You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats. To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind. Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

WhatsApp says this feature is “rolling out globally over the coming weeks.” So you might not see it right away, but even if you don’t, it should show up on your account soon.

Scheduled messages work not only for text, but also when sending media like photos and videos.

To get access to scheduled messages, make sure you’ve updated to the latest WhatsApp app update, which was just released today.

The 6.3-inch Fairphone 6 Plus features 12 user-replaceable parts, including the battery, screen, USB-C port, and cameras, all of which you can swap out with the included screwdriver. items.body:
A large light well brings daylight deep into this private [home](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/houses/) that was designed by [Desai Chia Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/desai-chia-architecture/) for a tight site in a dense [Maryland](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/maryland/) neighbourhood.

The project takes its name from its location in Bethesda, a city located northwest of Washington DC.

The house is set within a suburban neighbourhood near the downtown district, where residential lots are about one-fifth of an acre (647 square metres). Because the houses here are close together, the architects needed to be very mindful of privacy concerns.

### Drawings and photographs

Previous

Next

### Drawings and photographs

Close

- Basement and first floor plans
- Second and third floor plans
- Roof plan

“The clients sought a house that would feel open and light-filled without sacrificing privacy,” said New York-based [Desai Chia Architecture](https://www.desaichia.com/).

“Its compact lot and the close proximity of neighbouring houses required a careful response balancing both openness and discretion."

The architects intended the house to “rethink suburban-urban hybrid living through a modern lens”.

Roughly rectangular in plan, it has three levels and a basement. Setbacks help break up the mass, particularly on the street-facing elevation.

The building appears “as a two-storey building from several vantage points,” the team said.

“The home is carefully scaled to blend with neighbouring houses, balancing a strong architectural identity with sensitivity to its suburban context,” the team said.

Facades are clad in grey fibre-cement panels made to last for a century. The material is known for protecting against fire, pests and extreme weather, according to the team.

“A durable, low-maintenance exterior with a strong architectural presence was a key client priority from the outset,” the architects said.

“Glass-fibre-reinforced concrete (GRFC) panels were selected to create a crisp, sculptural facade that captures texture and shifting light throughout the day.”

[Read: Desai Chia uses "camouflaging effect" for secluded Osprey House in New York](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/11/27/desai-chia-camouflaging-effect-osprey-house-new-york/)

A modern-style bay window adds dimension and visual interest to the front and back facades.

Within the home, public spaces are located on the ground level. The rear portion opens into a yard with a lap pool.

The upper levels contain bedrooms and two offices, and the top floor has a rooftop terrace. The basement holds a gym, ping-pong area and media room.

A limited number of windows helps ensure privacy. To provide natural illumination, the team created a three-storey light well, which is positioned along a central staircase and brings daylight deep into the dwelling.

“This vertical, faceted volume allows sunlight to cascade downward, distributing diffuse light from a small skylight across circulation spaces on multiple levels while minimising solar heat gain,” Desai Chia Architecture said.

The all-electric house has a geothermal heating and cooling system. To enable the homeowners to age in place, the house has a shaft where an ADA-compliant elevator could be added in the future.

The homeowners are physicians, one of whom can walk to his practice in downtown Bethesda.

“When needed, the dedicated home offices allow both physicians to work from home in spaces with calming natural light,” the studio said.

“Its location – easily walkable to downtown amenities and robust public transit – supports a connected pattern of work and family life.”

Other homes in Maryland include a [restored carriage house by Colleen Healey Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/2022/06/09/colleen-healey-red-maple-house-maryland/) that features colourful facade panels and a [family home by Ziger Snead](https://www.dezeen.com/2018/08/27/slate-house-ziger-snead-architects-replaces-fire-ravaged-home-maryland/) clad in stone shingles, charred wood and weathering steel.

**Project credits:**

**Design architect:** Desai Chia Architecture
**Architect of record:** Thomson & Cooke Architects

# Liquid Sky Releases XEN FX LAB Audio Effects For iPad

Liquid Sky has released an iPad version of XEN FX LAB , its multi-effect plugin developed as a successor to the ZEN Delay Virtual software.

The iPad edition supports AUv3, allowing it to run as an effect inside compatible iOS music applications.

XEN FX LAB builds on the experimental delay approach of the earlier ZEN Delay Virtual, combining delay processing with filtering, overdrive, modulation, spring reverb and bit reduction. The iPad release brings the plugin’s sound-shaping tools to a touchscreen workflow and can be used within an AUv3-compatible host.

The desktop version of XEN FX LAB is also available for macOS and Windows. The iPad release is a separate App Store version.

Features:

- AUv3 audio effect for iPad
- Experimental delay processing
- Filtering and overdrive
- Modulation effects
- Spring reverb
- Bit reduction
- Designed as the successor to ZEN Delay Virtual
Pricing & Availability:

Liquid Sky XEN FX LAB is available for iPad on the App Store for an introductory price of €9.99, reduced from €17.99 through December 25, 2026.

# Google Home: November-Update bringt Verbesserungen für Gemini Live, Kameras und mehr

## Google Home: November-Update bringt Verbesserungen für Gemini Live, Kameras und mehr

von Carsten Knobloch 25. Nov. 2026 | 0

Google hat frische Release Notes für das eigene Smart-Home-Ökosystem veröffentlicht. Das Paket vom 25. November umfasst sowohl Anpassungen für Gemini for Home im Early Access als auch diverse Fehlerbehebungen und kleinere Funktionen für die Google-Home-App unter Android und iOS. Da müsst ihr mal schauen, ob etwas Nettes für euch dabei ist.

### Gemini for Home (Early Access)

Über die kommenden Wochen verteilt Google das bereits angekündigte Update für ein schnelleres und natürlicheres Gemini Live. Über den Sprachbefehl „Hey Google let’s chat“ lassen sich Unterhaltungen starten, wobei Gemini Live inzwischen auch alle alltäglichen Aktionen vom Stellen eines Timers bis zum Ausschalten der Beleuchtung abdeckt. Ab sofort startet auch die Funktion „Hey Google, tell me a story“ mit ausdrucksstärkeren Erzählerstimmen und dynamischem Tempo. Während einer Geschichte lässt sich der Verlauf per Zuruf anpassen, etwa mit „Hey Google, make the main character have magical powers“. Da hat Google leider nicht verraten, ob das nun 1:1 im Deutschen startet.

Bei der reinen Smart-Home-Steuerung hat Google nach eigener Aussage an der Geschwindigkeit gedreht. Die Performance-Verbesserungen für gängige Gerätebefehle sind mittlerweile vollständig ausgerollt, sodass Antworten und Aktionen flotter reagieren. Dazu kommen zwei Fehlerbehebungen im Alltag: Gemini verliert bei Rückfragen wie „turn them back on“ nach dem Ausschalten der Wohnzimmerlampen nicht mehr so leicht den Kontext und antwortet beim Stoppen von Musik oder Medien seltener fälschlicherweise mit „nothing is playing“. Wer auf unterstützten Smart Displays Fragen stellt, die aus dem Web beantwortet werden, kann über die neue Schaltfläche „Sources“ die zugrunde liegenden Websites einsehen. U.2- und M.2-SSD-Erweiterung: U.2-SSD-Unterstützung in Schacht 1 und 2 ermöglicht... −24% 499,98 EUR Bei Amazon ansehen Google Home App: Kameras In der Google-Home-App steht das Feedback zu Videoclips in unterstützten Regionen jetzt auch Haushalten mit mehreren Administratoren zur Verfügung. Neben allgemeinem Feedback zur Fehlerbehebung lassen sich auf Wunsch auch die Clips selbst teilen, um das Videoverständnis von Gemini for Home zu trainieren. Für die Nest Cam Outdoor (kabelgebunden, 2. Generation) sowie die hierzulande nicht regulär erhältlichen US-Modelle onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In und onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired gibt es in der Live-Ansicht nun eine Fernsteuerung, mit der sich eine 30 Sekunden lange Sicherheits-Sirene aktivieren und wieder stoppen lässt. Die beiden genannten onn-Kameras unterstützen mit einem aktiven Google-Home-Premium-Abo jetzt auch Benachrichtigungen für bekannte Gesichter (Familiar Faces).

Für Android-Nutzer räumt das Update gleich drei Fehler aus dem Weg:

- Unter Android 17 erscheinen bei Kamera-Benachrichtigungen von Breitbild-Kameras von Nest und Partnern wieder Video-Vorschauen und Vorschaubilder.
- Beim Abspielen des ereignisbasierten Videoverlaufs treten laut Google weniger Wiedergabefehler („Couldn't play video“) auf.
- Auf Pixel-Smartphones überlagern Bedienelemente und Ereignisbeschreibungen in der Vollbild-Queransicht nicht mehr die Aussparung der Frontkamera.
### Licht, Thermostate und Google Home Premium

Unter iOS hat Google das Farbrad für die Lichtsteuerung überarbeitet, damit sich voll gesättigte Farben wieder leichter auswählen lassen. Für Besitzer eines Nest Learning Thermostat (4. Generation) oder des regulären Nest Thermostat gibt es eine Neuerung bei den Zeitplänen: Ein Tagesplan für die Temperatur lässt sich in der App kopieren und direkt auf mehrere Wochentage übertragen.

Für Abonnenten von Google Home Premium in den USA vereinfacht sich die Einrichtung neuer Kameras. Statt jede Premium-Funktion einzeln konfigurieren zu müssen, lassen sich alle Funktionen in einem Schritt aktivieren. Bestehende Einstellungen bereits vorhandener Kameras bleiben dabei unverändert, und einzelne Kameras oder Funktionen können vor Abschluss des Setups weiterhin angepasst oder abgewählt werden. Für uns ja nicht relevant.

# iZotope’s Nectar 5 brings lyrics-based editing to its vocal production suite

Featured Deal

## iZotope’s Nectar 5 brings lyrics-based editing to its vocal production suite

The vocal plugin suite adds a transcription-driven effects tool, plus a new Serial Compressor and a retuned Vocal Assistant.

iZotope has launched Nectar 5, the latest edition of its vocal production suite. It introduces Moments, an ARA plugin that transcribes a vocal into lyrics in dozens of languages and lets users apply effects to selected words and phrases.

Once the vocal is transcribed, producers can add effects such as reverb throws, doubling and formant shifts to specific words and phrases rather than drawing the automation by hand. iZotope calls it an industry first for ARA-compatible DAWs.

### Two new modules and a retuned Vocal Assistant

Nectar 5 also adds two new modules. Serial Compressor lets you stack up to three compressors at once, to tame peaks while reinforcing the body of your vocal. This keeps the vocal upfront in the mix without over-compressing. It defaults to a FET-into-Opto setup which iZotope says professional engineers love. Vocal stabilizer is an adaptive EQ with two modes: Shape moves a vocal towards a more polished tonal balance, while Cut tames unwanted resonances. It also offers multiband control, with per-band Amount settings and adjustable crossover.

The Vocal Assistant, which builds a vocal chain in a single click, has been retuned to offer a better starting point. A new Custom Flow option gives users more control over the result. They can set the style, register, key, modules, Intensity and Atmosphere, or load an acapella reference for vocal matching.

An Overview page also joins the line-up, offering key controls for Nectar’s core processors with shortcuts to each module for finer adjustments.

Micro Pitch Shift gains a Dimension mode, which spreads and subtly detunes a vocal to add width and weight. Reverb, Delay and Dimension now have a Wet Level control and 3-band filters, plus easy ducking for Reverb and Delay.

The full suite includes 12 full modules and two mini-modules along with Moments, Breath Control, Melodyne Essential, the Mothership channel-strip plugin and more than 400 presets. It also includes 14 component plugins that can be used in other vocal chains.

### Pricing

Nectar 5 is currently on Cyber Sale for £175, down from £239, with the sale running until December 7. Existing iZotope customers can see crossgrade and upgrade pricing by logging in to the iZotope website.

For more information, or to purchase Nectar 5 visit iZotope.com .

*Piaget’s second collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts translates the pop artist’s 1986 Camouflage self-portraits into dials made of gemstone marquetry.*

## Related Articles

### What Is Internet Cinema?

[↗ Primärquelle: artnews.com](https://www.artnews.com/art-news/artists/what-is-internet-cinema-1234807781/)

### Christie's Adds UK Auction House Dreweatts to Its Portfolio

[↗ Primärquelle: artnews.com](https://www.artnews.com/art-news/market/christies-adds-uk-auction-house-dreweatts-to-portfolio-1234807665/)

Long before luxury watches were as sought after as they are today, Andy Warhol coveted and collected them. Over the course of the 1960s, ’70s, and ’80s, the Pop Art pioneer amassed more than 300 timepieces that reflected his high-low tastes. He collected watches the way he collected everything, with an appetite that blurred connoisseurship and compulsion. When Sotheby’s sold his estate in 1988, the sale featured timepieces by Cartier, Bulgari, and Patek Philippe alongside cookie jars and Art Deco furniture. Warhol is often said to have worn watches less to tell time than to be seen in them. For an artist who made a career of elevating the ordinary, a watch was a portable piece of pop culture, a status symbol he could wear and treasure.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

One brand, however, stood out. Warhol owned at least seven wristwatches by the Swiss maison, Piaget. Founded in 1874 in La Côte-aux-Fées, a village in the heart of Switzerland’s Jura mountain range, the house was renowned in the latter half of the 20th century for its creative selection of timepieces in unusual shapes, many featuring dials made of exotic ornamental stones. One of those watches, a quartz-powered reference 15102 model that Warhol purchased from the brand in 1973, now forms the foundation for a Piaget collection bound to appeal to lovers of art in general and fans of Warhol’s revolutionary oeuvre in particular.

Housed in an 18-karat gold, 45 mm cushion-shaped case designed by Jean-Claude Gueit, Piaget’s then artistic director, the striking piece, which was part of a limited series manufactured between 1972 and 1977, featured a black onyx dial. Fittingly, it was called the Black Tie. In 1988, Piaget purchased Warhol’s watch at Sotheby’s landmark sale.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

The artist’s choice of Piaget was no accident. In the 1950s and ’60s, the house had built its reputation on extreme thinness, introducing ultra-thin movements that transformed the watches into slim, supple pieces of jewelry. By the 1960s, Piaget had paired that technical prowess with a bolder sensibility: gold bracelets, vivid hardstone dials, and silhouettes that owed more to the jeweler’s bench than to the watchmaker’s. The result was a crossover brand that suited the decade’s appetite for spectacle. For Warhol, who drew no line between commerce and art, a watch that doubled as a gem-set object was irresistible. The Black Tie’s onyx dial, as sleek and dark as a lacquered cigarette case, could not have been better suited to the man who documented the era’s elite so closely.

Twenty-six years after Piaget purchased the Black Tie, the brand used the occasion of its 140th anniversary in 2014 to create a revival collection called Black Tie Vintage. The line caused such a stir among Piaget’s clientele that in 2024, for its sesquicentennial, the maison decided to up the ante. Thanks to a collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts, Piaget was given the rights to rename the Black Tie Vintage watch after Warhol himself.

**From Collage to Camouflage**

The first collaborative watch to emerge from Piaget’s work with the foundation was the 2025 Collage, a limited edition of 50 pieces featuring an artful composition of ornamental stones—yellow Namibian serpentine, pink opal, and green chrysoprase—inspired by Warhol’s Polaroids. This month, Piaget has introduced a second piece, which also uses ornamental stone marquetry, this time to pay tribute to the *Camouflage* self-portraits that Warhol created in 1986.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

“When you buy it, you don’t only buy a watch, you buy a whole story and heritage,” Jean-Bernard Forot, Piaget’s head of patrimony, tells *ARTnews*. “You can, of course, talk about the material, what it does for you. But at the same time, you have to talk about Warhol, you have to talk about Piaget, you have to talk about art.”

Limited to 86 pieces, after the year in which Warhol created the eight-print *Camouflage* series, the watch, whose dial combines the ornamental stones sodalite and turquoise with satin-finished yellow gold and polished rose gold, faithfully interprets the artist’s work without blindly mimicking it.

“Camouflage is very difficult to work on, even in design, because we don’t just copy and paste the artwork—we have to find another way to express camouflage,” Forot says.

Among the final serial group of paintings Warhol completed before his untimely death in 1987, the works paid homage to the military-inspired camouflage pattern, originally intended to help soldiers blend in with their surroundings. In Warhol’s hands, they became a comment on Abstract Expressionism, not to mention a deeply personal statement on his lifelong effort to conceal his true self beneath wigs, makeup, and a carefully constructed facade.

Photo Courtesy of Piaget

Printed in acid brights across enormous canvases, the swirling forms feature in self-portraits overlayed with Warhol’s face, framed by his signature shock of hair. For an artist who spent his life hiding in plain sight, the *Camouflage* series is arguably his most meta work.

In order to capture the essence of the paintings on the face of a watch, Piaget’s artisans took some liberties with color. Rather than emphasizing Warhol’s use of yellow, for example, they highlighted the brand’s use of turquoise, Forot says.

# The efficiency paradox: Why greener AI means more waste

November 25, 2026

## The efficiency paradox: Why greener AI means more waste

edited by Lisa Lock , reviewed by Andrew Zinin

Lisa Lock

Scientific Editor

Andrew Zinin

Chief Editor

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

fact-checked

trusted source

written by researcher(s)

proofread

AI is increasingly being promoted as a solution to climate change. It can help companies use less fuel, reduce waste and make production more efficient.

For example, AI can help delivery companies plan more efficient routes, reducing the fuel they use and the emissions they produce. Similar savings could be made across other industries and transport networks, potentially reducing the overall environmental impact. But greater efficiency can also encourage more consumption.

AI is being promoted as a climate solution and as a driver of competitiveness, productivity and economic growth. The World Trade Organization estimates that the widespread adoption of AI could increase global trade by around 40% by 2040 . This is generally presented as a benefit.

But there is an obvious contradiction here. If AI makes firms more efficient and profitable, it encourages further investment and expansion. Successful firms do not use productivity gains to produce less, but to expand and to make greater profits.

When these dynamics are generalized across the economy, the result is more production, transportation, resource extraction, consumption and ultimately more environmental destruction.

This is capitalism's efficiency paradox , known as the Jevons paradox. According to William Stanley Jevons, a 19th-century English economist, any increase in resource efficiency generates an increase in long-term resource consumption, rather than a decrease.

New technologies can help businesses produce more goods using less energy, materials and labor. But by making production cheaper and faster, they can also encourage businesses to make and sell more, increasing the total amount of resources that people use.

Industrial efficiency gains have been a defining feature of capitalism since the Industrial Revolution. Steam-powered textile mills and coal mines in the late 18th century, the Bessemer steel process (making steel by blowing air through molten iron) in the 19th century, and Henry Ford's car assembly line in the 20th all dramatically increased efficiency.

Yet none of these efficiency gains reduced society's overall consumption of resources. Rather, they underpinned successive waves of industrial expansion, fossil-fuel use and environmental degradation.

AI is no different.

My research shows how digital technologies provide a historical example of this dynamic.

For decades, improvements in computers, telecommunications and data storage have allowed companies to spread different stages of production across several countries. They can now use real-time digital networks to share information and coordinate manufacturing and trade around the world.

These technologies have made possible today's highly integrated global supply chains, allowing firms to source components from thousands of suppliers and move goods across continents with extraordinary speed and precision.

The environmental consequences are immense.

Digital technologies have helped companies produce and sell more goods around the world. This has increased the demand for raw materials, pollution from transport and damage to the natural environment. International trade in goods is now linked to around 30% of threats to the world's species .

Rather than reversing these trends, AI is deepening them. It is making supply chains faster, more responsive and more geographically extensive. From a business perspective, this is progress. Environmentally, it accelerates ecological breakdown.

## Cleaner technology, more fossil fuels

The same contradiction can be seen in the energy sector. Much discussion of AI and green technology assumes that cleaner technologies replace dirtier ones. Yet, as the historian Jean-Baptiste Fressoz shows , new energy systems tend to accumulate on top of rather than substitute for each other.

Wood, coal, oil, gas and renewables have largely been added to one another rather than replacing one another. Green technologies are making fossil-fuel industries more efficient, rather than replacing them.

Many of the technologies being promoted as climate solutions, including AI, are actually accelerating the extraction of fossil fuels that is driving climate change.

In Guyana, since commercial oil production began in 2019, the country has become one of the world's fastest-growing producers of oil, with targets to produce 1.3 million barrels per day by 2027. AI-enabled drilling and "geosteering"—the real-time adjustment of a well's path to keep it within oil-bearing rock—are increasing the rate of oil extraction.

So, can a technology designed to increase productivity, competitiveness and growth solve a crisis rooted in relentless profit-oriented expansion of production and consumption on a finite planet? Until that question is confronted, greener AI is likely to make ecological destruction more efficient rather than bring it to an end.

Lisa Lock

BA art history, MA material culture. Former museum editor, paramedic, and transplant coordinator. Editing for Science X since 2021. Full profile →

Andrew Zinin

Master's in physics with research experience. Long-time science news enthusiast. Plays key role in Science X's editorial success. Full profile →

# Konkurrenz für Fender & Co.? Japanische Traditionsmarke ab sofort in Deutschland verfügbar

## Bacchus Guitars jetzt bei Hyperactive, E-Gitarren und Bässe

## Japanische Gitarrenbaukunst kommt nach Deutschland

Bacchus Guitars

Bacchus Guitars ist ein japanischer Hersteller für E-Gitarren und E-Bässe. Die sorgfältig zusammengestellten Instrumente sind jetzt über Hyperactive Audiotechnik in Deutschland erhältlich.

## Bacchus Guitars: Jetzt bei Hyperactive erhältlich

Bacchus Guitars steht für die Kombination von japanischer Handwerkskunst und moderner Fertigung. Die Marke bietet Instrumente in verschiedenen Preisklassen vom Einsteiger-Bass bis zur handgefertigten Premium-Gitarre an. Hinter Bacchus steht der Traditionshersteller Deviser mit Sitz in Matsumoto in der Präfektur Nagano. Dessen Geschichte geht bis ins Jahr 1977 zurück, als der legendäre japanische Gitarrenbauer Yasuo Momose zusammen mit einem kleinen Team die Akustikgitarren-Marke Headway ins Leben rief.

Heute stellt Deviser unter verschiedenen Labels hochwertige Instrumente her, unter anderem im hauseigenen Custom Shop namens „Aska Workshop“, wo die Bacchus Handmade Series gefertigt wird.

Bacchus hat moderne Gitarren, darunter unter anderem S-Type- und T-Type-Modelle sowie J-Bässe und P-Bässe, im Portfolio. Der deutsche Vertrieb Hyperactive Audiotechnik hat die japanische Marke jetzt ins Programm aufgenommen. Neben Händlern können dort auch Privatkunden Instrumente kaufen.

## Preis und Verfügbarkeit

Japanische Instrumente genießen seit jeher einen guten Ruf! Die Instrumente von Bacchus sind also allemal einen Blick wert! Die Preise reichen von etwas über 300 Euro für Einsteigermodelle bis hin zu knappen 4.000 Euro für Modelle aus der Premiumlinie.

items.body:
# The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.

If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

“The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”

The decision, announced a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.

## A long deployment runway

This announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the company wide latitude as it works through these remaining issues.

For example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.

The authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The company sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

The FCC did not grant this waiver request “because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements.” The company will need to obtain a waiver before deploying any Starmind satellites that are not intended to be disposed of via atmospheric reentry.

However, in other ways the FCC appears to have been incredibly lenient with SpaceX. This is particularly the case with environmental concerns raised by numerous parties that commented on SpaceX’s application to the FCC.

## Dismisses environmental concerns

Half a dozen organizations, such as the Secure World Foundation and American Astronomical Society, raised concerns about deploying so many satellites into orbit, citing collision risks, orbital debris, atmospheric pollution from so many satellite reentries, impacts on astronomical observations, and more. The FCC also received approximately 1,500 public comments concerning SpaceX’s application.

Some of these environmental issues, the FCC said, lay beyond the scope of its review. For example, on concerns about the environmental implications of thousands or potentially tens of thousands of rocket launches, the FCC said, “Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview.”

The FCC also rejected calls for further environmental scrutiny of pollution from satellite reentries, including concerns about aluminum oxides and their potential effects on the ozone layer. “Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record,” the FCC authorization states.

As part of its decision, the FCC cited a significant policy change adopted in October, when the agency concluded that space-based activities generally fall outside its obligations under the National Environmental Policy Act. The FCC reasoned that as these activities occur beyond US territory, they don’t constitute federal actions requiring environmental review. As a result, the agency declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental assessment of SpaceX’s Starmind constellation.

items.body:
Parisa Khoshnami at *Aeon*:

Photo by Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/via Getty Images

What is happening in Tehran now is the quiet discarding of rules that have governed daily life for decades. A few inches of [visible hair](https://aeon.co/videos/in-an-act-of-resistance-elahe-forgoes-a-hijab-at-a-family-party) used to be the whole argument, but it is no longer the point. Women up and down the city are removing their scarves and manteaus – the loose, knee-length coats they were required to wear over their clothes in public – and adopting the latest trends: capri trousers, cropped and close-fitting clothes, bare arms, midi skirts, bare legs. Enjoying this new freedom, they parade along Iranshahr (rather aptly, the street takes its name from the old Persian word for the land of the Iranians), where shops that used to sell manteaus and headscarves have switched to blouses and T-shirts.

A young woman whom I’ll call Mina puts the shift in blunter terms. ‘It isn’t optional anymore,’ she said. ‘You cannot leave the house in ordinary clothes. You have to be put together.’ She does not wear a headscarf anymore, and nor does anyone she goes out with. On the streets where people go to be seen, she tells me, hardly anyone does. In Tehran, those who can afford it wear the latest designer clothing. But in small Iranian towns, local workshops turn out such good copies of the latest Parisian and New York trends that anyone can now dress head to toe in ‘Chanel’, whatever their class.

More [↗ aeon.co](https://aeon.co/essays/its-not-political-the-young-fashionistas-of-tehran).

items.body:
On the northwestern tip of France's Noirmoutier Island, behind the 19th-century Church of the Sacred Heart, a small cemetery overlooks the Atlantic Ocean. Beyond its stone walls stretch the waters of the Bay of Biscay, with the tiny island of Le Pilier visible on the horizon. Many of those buried here were sailors and fishermen whose lives were intimately connected to the sea.

Among the traditional graves stands a striking row of white Commonwealth headstones, commemorating the victims of a largely forgotten maritime tragedy.

On June 17, 1940, as British troops and civilians were being evacuated from France, German aircraft bombed the British troopship HMT Lancastria off the coast of Saint-Nazaire. The ship sank within minutes, taking thousands of lives in one of the deadliest maritime disasters of World War II.

In the following days, the Atlantic currents carried the bodies of victims onto the French coastline, including the shores of Noirmoutier.

Today, the cemetery contains 40 Commonwealth war burials, 22 of them unidentified. Most were victims of the Lancastria disaster.

Overlooking the very ocean that claimed so many lives, L'Herbaudière's marine cemetery remains a peaceful yet poignant reminder of the island's maritime heritage and the tragedies of war.

items.body:
# Collien Monica Fernandes: "Paradiesische Zustände für Täter"

## Orange Day - Gewalt gegen Frauen : Collien Monica Fernandes: "Paradiesische Zustände für Täter"

Niedrige Aufklärungsraten und bleiernes Schweigen: Bei ZDFheute live spricht Collien Monica Fernandes über zunehmende Gewalt gegen Frauen und was sich in Deutschland ändern muss.

Immer mehr Frauen werden Opfer von häuslicher und digitaler Gewalt. Warum steigen die Zahlen in Deutschland und wie können Frauen besser geschützt werden? ZDFheute live analysiert.

Moderatorin und Schauspielerin Collien Monica Fernandes nahm zum Orange Day an einer Demo in Berlin teil. Der internationale Orange Day soll Gewalt gegen Frauen ins Bewusstsein rücken und zum Kampf dagegen aufrufen. Bei ZDFheute live spricht sie über Gewalt gegen Frauen in Deutschland. Ihrem Ex-Partner, dem Schauspieler Christian Ulmen, hatte sie schwere Vorwürfe gemacht: Laut Fernandes hat er Fake-Profile in ihrem Namen erstellt und darüber pornografische Darstellungen verbreitet. Für Ulmen gilt die Unschuldsvermutung.

Frauen hätten diesen Erfahrungen gemacht und trotzdem gebe es viele Männer, die diese Realität nicht wahrhaben wollen, sagt Collien Fernandes. Es sei wichtig, dass Männer nicht wegsehen.

Sehen Sie das ganze Interview oben im Video oder lesen Sie hier Auszüge:

ZDFheute live: Wie können Männer in unserer Gesellschaft dazu beitragen, dass die Frauen sicherer leben?

Collien Monica Fernandes: "Was mich sehr erstaunt hat, nachdem meine Geschichte publiziert wurde, ist das relativierende Feedback vor allem von Männern. Ich denke, es fängt erstmal mit dem Zuhören an, wenn Frauen ihre Realitäten schildern. (...) Die Frauen haben selbst diesen Erfahrungswert und trotzdem gibt es so viele Männer, die diese Frauenrealität nicht wahrhaben wollen."

ZDFheute live: Wie viel Unterstützung würden Sie sich wünschen von den Männern?

Fernandes: "Von dem, wie ich es bisher wahrgenommen habe, waren die Männer meistens deutlich in der Unterzahl. Ich habe mich dann sehr gefreut, als am Vatertag eine Männerdemo organisiert worden ist, beziehungsweise zwei, eine in Berlin und eine in Hamburg. Ich glaube, dass es total wichtig ist, dass die Männer ebenfalls auf die Straße gehen, dass die Männer laut sind, was diese Thematik angeht, und dass die Männer vor allem nicht wegsehen.

> Wir hätten weit weniger Taten, wenn Männer sich involvieren würden, wenn Männer im richtigen Moment den Mund aufmachen. „

Collien Monica Fernandes

ZDFheute live : Was meinen Sie mit "paradiesische Zustände" für die Täter?

Fernandes: "Es herrschen tatsächlich paradiesische Zustände für Täter in Deutschland. Das zeigen die Zahlen ganz klar. Wenn wir auf Vergewaltigung schauen, dann hat man eine 99-prozentige Chance, davonzukommen. Schätzungsweise nur ein Prozent aller Vergewaltiger wird verurteilt. Und auch bei der häuslichen Gewalt reden wir von einer mickrigen einstelligen Zahl. Es ist de facto nicht so, dass 99 Prozent der Frauen sich so etwas ausdenken, und deshalb brauchen wir einfach ein besseres System, ein funktionierendes Rechtssystem, das die Frauen schützt, das die Opfer schützt und nicht die Täter."

Verona Pooth hat über ihre eigenen Erfahrungen mit digitaler sexualisierter Gewalt gesprochen. Sie habe immer wieder gefälschte Bilder von sich geschickt bekommen.

Das Interview führte Sara Bildau.
